look_here_first: SHORTSPIKE WINDMILLGRASS is the accepted seed-producing natural hybrid of Chloris cucullata × C. verticillata, documented in USDA NRCS Welder Germplasm accession 9085260 / PI 645601. The installed windmill photo is still a SOURCE-LABELLED candidate, not a voucher. Check longish 5–16 one-sided racemes, upper sterile oblong lemma ~1.7–2.2 mm and shorter ~1–2 mm awn versus fertile lemma ~2.2–2.9 mm with ~2–5 mm awn on the SAME specimen. Parent images don't prove hybrid identity. Macro-voucher hold stays.

kew_diagnostic.habit: Perennial, often stoloniferous, 30–70 cm tall, flattened keeled sheaths, ciliate membrane ligule about 2 mm.
kew_diagnostic.racemes: 5–16 digitate/unilateral racemes, each about 3–17.6 cm; whorls may vary, no sole-head hybrid proof.
kew_diagnostic.fertile_lemma: 2.2–2.9 mm long; short subapical awn about 2–5 mm.
kew_diagnostic.sterile_lemma: Upper barren lemma 1.7–2.2 mm, typically oblong NOT big rounded hood, its own awn 1–2 mm.
kew_diagnostic.field_protocol: Photograph same intact seedhead and 2 discrete lemmas and awns with 1 mm scale. Comparison to actual parents is educational, not individual hybrid verification.

published_floristic_key_20261022.source: Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae/Chloris key and species description, p. 1256
published_floristic_key_20261022.diagnostic: Upper sterile floret commonly squared off and nearly as wide as long, sometimes triangular; the upper margins of the lower (fertile) lemmas lack a prominent tuft of hairs. The lower fertile lemma is 2.2–2.9 mm long and not conspicuously one-sided swollen (not gibbous).
published_floristic_key_20261022.limits: Morphology overlaps C. cucullata and C. verticillata, and the historical key alone cannot establish a single photographed individual as the hybrid.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Shortspike windmillgrass — source candidate, measured floret requirements, scientific hold
steps: 1 · FIELD PHOTO (PANEL 0): the documented CC BY hand-scale picture shows a hub and narrow one-sided racemes, but no diagnostic individual hybrid floret or roots. Existing two arrows are gross-only.

2 · BOTANICAL DRAWING (PANEL 1): historical Hitchcock/Chase page, figure 768 for C. subdolichostachya while figure 770 is C. cucullata. This is NOT a photograph or voucher of the photographed candidate.
3 · ACTUAL PARENTS (PANELS 2 AND 3): hooded and tumble windmillgrass are different species; do not recaption either as this hybrid.
4 · SPECIMEN BASE: find the actual rooted perennial crown and physical rooting stolon nodes plus complete connected flowering shoot. This is not present in the photos.
5 · TRUE LIGULE: open the INNER blade–sheath junction, distinguish membranous fringe from sheath hairs and measure about 2-mm literature value using physical 1-mm ruler.

6 · SPIKELET KEY: dissect one mature source-verified spikelet; keep two glumes, a 2.2–2.9-mm fertile lemma with 2–5-mm awn and a 1.7–2.2-mm oblong upper sterile lemma with separate 1–2-mm awn. These are Kew ranges, not photographic measurements.

7 · HOLD: if the measured reproductive combination and specimen provenance are missing, retain Chloris sp. in field records and keep the source photograph a hybrid candidate; do not misreport a parent or release image as hybrid proof.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · WHAT WE REALLY HAVE
field_id_short_tiles.short: A photographed windmill candidate, NOT confirmed hybrid anatomy
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 0 is an actual photographer-labelled C. × subdolichostachya flowering head. The photo visibly shows about a wheel of purple narrow one-sided spikelet-bearing rays attached at a common hub. Its 2 original arrows mark real gross structures, but there is NO true 1-mm spikelet scale, no demonstrated sterile lemma outline, no exposed collar/root or linked field voucher. Keep the original identification as a CANDIDATE and refer to Chloris sp. if field diagnosis cannot be completed.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED HABIT AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Stoloniferous perennial in published description; not photographed here
field_id_short_tiles.details: GrassBase/Kew describes a perennial with stolons, mostly basal leaves, flattened keeled sheaths and a true ciliate membrane ligule approximately 2 mm long. NONE of these anatomical structures is resolved in the installed hand-held seedhead photograph. Needed: taxonomically authenticated living candidate with a rooted crown, connected stolon and visibly rooting nodes, complete attached flowering stem and an opened inner blade–sheath ligule beside a metric ruler. Do not borrow the parent's collar photograph and attribute it to a confirmed hybrid.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · DISSECT A MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Separate the two glumes, fertile lemma and smaller sterile lemma
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published Kew treatment gives mature spikelets approximately 2–3 mm, lower glume about 1.5–2.5 mm and upper glume about 2–3 mm. The existing hand-scale photograph cannot resolve either glume, and the HISTORICAL public-domain plate (panel 1) is an illustration across DIFFERENT species, not the actual plant. Use 10–20× or more, detach one mature voucher-derived spikelet, and photograph individual glumes with 1-mm reference. Do not count illustrations as photographs.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · THE TWO AWNS ARE DIFFERENT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma ~2.2–2.9 mm with 2–5 mm awn; sterile ~1.7–2.2 mm with 1–2 mm awn
field_id_short_tiles.details: Measure LEMMA BODY separately from the projecting AWN. Kew GrassBase characterizes a 2.2–2.9 mm fertile lemma bearing its own 2–5 mm awn, then an upper oblong sterile lemma about 1.7–2.2 mm with a separate 1–2 mm awn. These values are literature, NOT measurements made on the photographed candidate. At 20× or greater, show both complete free lemmas and their origins from ONE opened and authenticated spikelet, with physical 1-mm calibration. Awning a detached unlabelled glume or citing the parent's longer awn is not valid confirmation.
field_id_short_tiles.status: DECISIVE PAIRED REAL LEMMA MACROS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · COMPARE BOTH PARENTS WITHOUT MIXING THEM UP
field_id_short_tiles.short: Hooded + tumble photos are explicitly two DIFFERENT species
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 2 is actual Chloris cucullata (hooded windmillgrass), whose upper sterile lemma is commonly round/inflated and short-awned; its Fonseca image ALSO contains a separate left-hand plume that must not be declared hooded. Panel 3 is actual Chloris verticillata (tumble windmillgrass), generally bearing more separated raceme tiers and longer fertile/sterile awns. Neither parent image is an actual verified hybrid. Kew accepts C. cucullata × C. verticillata as the hybrid taxon; the photo-level diagnosis still needs a mature specimen and expert comparison.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PARENT COMPARISON PHOTOS AVAILABLE — candidate not verified

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · HOW TO CLEAR THE SCIENTIFIC HOLD
field_id_short_tiles.short: Authenticated voucher + four-role specimen series + proper rights
field_id_short_tiles.details: Required: 1) independent taxonomist/herbarium voucher determination for a candidate with source locality; 2) same photographed living plant showing actual rooted base, attached flowering head and inner ciliate ligule with mm scale; 3) mature separated real spikelet with both glumes, fertile lemma plus awn, upper sterile lemma plus awn; 4) reference comparison with voucher-backed C. cucullata and C. verticillata. Retain the candidate's individual CC BY attribution and the historical public-domain plate's figure 768/770 labels. Do not use NRCS Welder Germplasm release field photos without an independently reviewed image license. A 2006 release establishes the hybrid as real, not this individual photo. Require mobile Pages and photo-arrow review before PUBLIC_READY.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SCIENTIFIC HOLD — DO NOT CERTIFY AS CONFIRMED HYBRID
